gauntlet: question
The existing resolver is the better fit because it already owns every report-view default (settings/resolver.ts:12), and the view already reads its values from that resolver (ui/report-view.ts:30). I traced that resolver-to-view path end to end. A new key there gets the existing defaulting and resolution behavior and adds no new read path. A view-local object would create a second settings path beside the owning one: defaults would be split across two places, and the view would need its own merge logic. I've recorded this in the draft: `Settings ownership: existing resolver (settings/resolver.ts:12 -> ui/report-view.ts:30)`.

Next, what the setting controls. Today, report filters stay active across a workspace switch and can hide rows in the new workspace. What should happen to active filters when the workspace changes?
A) The setting controls the reset, defaulting to clearing filters on a switch. The reported hidden-rows case is fixed by default, and users can opt to keep filters.
B) The setting controls the reset, defaulting to keeping filters as today. Current behavior is unchanged, and users opt in to clearing.
C) Other - name it (for example, keep only the filters that still match fields in the new workspace).
Recommendation: A - the reported problem is rows hidden after a switch, so the default should fix it, while the setting keeps today's behavior available for users who rely on it.

gauntlet: question
Reusing the resolver is the better fit because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. That keeps one settings contract and one data path; a view-local object would introduce a second owner for behavior the existing path can supply.

Filter-reset behavior is still undecided. Which behavior should the new setting default to when switching workspaces?
A) Reset report filters so filters from the previous workspace cannot hide rows.
B) Preserve active report filters, with resetting available through the setting.
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - it addresses the hidden-row problem you described while allowing users to choose preservation.
